_comment: One disposition and one owner for every Dockerfile in the repository (#346). PUBLISHED = pushed to a registry by release.yml. DISTRIBUTED = built from this repo by an operator or a shipped script, and possibly pushed to the operator's own registry, but never published by us. INTERNAL = built only by this repository's own CI or test tooling and never run outside it; must justify itself in prose. RETIRED = superseded; names what replaced_by it and the issue that owns its removal. PUBLISHED and DISTRIBUTED must name `built_by` and `scanned_by` jobs that exist, OR carry a `coverage_exception` naming an owner, an issue and a reason -- version-scoped and owned, per #346's AC-4, because an exception nobody owns is just an exemption. Checked by scripts/check-image-inventory.py: every Dockerfile on disk appears exactly once, no entry names a Dockerfile that is gone, and adding an image without its jobs (or an owned exception) fails CI -- that is the point. A PUBLISHED entry claiming `published_digest_verified: true` is machine-checked against the publishing job's wiring (#611, #346 AC-5): release.yml's images job must build each image exactly once into its `-rc` quarantine repository, scan the candidate digest with Trivy (HIGH/CRITICAL, exit-code 1) and Grype (--fail-on high --only-fixed) -- the same policy security.yml enforces on PRs and nightlies -- apply the release tags (version, X.Y, latest) to that scanned digest via `docker buildx imagetools create` only after both scans pass, and cosign-sign that same digest, so the digest the scans admit is the digest the release publishes and the signature attests. History: #593 recorded this gap as `published_digest_verified: false` because release.yml rebuilt independently of security.yml's scanned candidates; #349 had already closed the mutable-base half (every base/tool image reference is digest-pinned in quality/image-pins.json, checked by scripts/check-image-pins.py, and release.yml's images job refuses a release whose provenance attestation does not name every pinned base digest); #611 closed the rebuild half by making the release path single-build. Both flags above were flipped only together with that re-wiring, and the gate re-reads the wiring on every run -- re-introducing a second build, a pre-scan release tag, an unsigned digest or a scan that never admits the published digest flips the claim back to what it would then honestly be: a failure.

images.rationale: The maistro-engine API image. Chainguard/Wolfi runtime, browser surface deliberately split out into Dockerfile.research so this one can go near-zero-CVE.
The Agent Conductor image: frontend build plus a Chainguard/Wolfi runtime over a self-contained venv.

The RESEARCH worker: browser-use + Playwright + Chromium on a Debian base. Its own header calls the browser surface 'the single largest remaining CVE source', which is why it was split out of the API image -- so it is the image that most needs scanning, and was the one not scanned. Operators build it where the web tool actually runs; nothing pushes it, so there is no published digest to sign.

Full-isolation RSI runner: the entire self-improvement loop executes inside it and agent-authored code only ever runs there, so its contents are a containment boundary rather than a convenience. Built by tools/run_rsi_isolated.sh and tools/run_rsi_evolve_isolated.sh on an operator's machine; never pushed.

Docker Sandboxes template, and a shipped operator artifact rather than an internal one: deploy/sbx/build.sh is a documented command, its PUSH_TAG path runs `docker push`, and docs/install/sandbox-sbx.md tells operators to build or push it for real RSI workloads. It also executes agent-authored code, which makes it the image whose contents matter most. Calling it INTERNAL exempted it from the coverage this gate exists to enforce (Codex, #593).

coverage_exception.reason: CI cannot build it from a checkout alone: it is FROM docker/sandbox-templates:shell-docker and copies preseed tars that deploy/sbx/build.sh produces in the same run. Wiring the preseed step into the containers job is real work and is tracked on #346; recording the exception is what keeps it visible instead of letting a wrong disposition hide it.

images.rationale: The image RSI's nested test containers run under --network=none, built and shipped by the same deploy/sbx/build.sh pass as sbx-template. Same operator-facing status, same reason it is not INTERNAL.

coverage_exception.reason: Shares sbx-template's preseed precondition and its owner.

images.rationale: Five lines: pytest and httpx over the e2e directory. Built only by packages/hive-conductor/docker-compose.test.yml's api-tests service, runs only this repository's own tests, never leaves CI or a developer's machine.
The browser half of the same e2e harness, built only by docker-compose.test.yml's playwright service. Same reasoning as hive-conductor-e2e-api.
Copier Jinja template for generated autonoetic products. Rendered into downstream repos at scaffold time; this repository does not build or run it.
